candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — laboratory-test interpretation
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — serum total protein
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize serum total protein as a nonspecific laboratory measure that helps evaluate abnormal protein states and requires clinical correlation.

options.A: It identifies one specific disease by itself, so an abnormal value does not require any other testing or clinical correlation.
options.B: It directly measures glomerular filtration rate and is used as the primary stand-alone test of kidney filtration.
options.C: It can help identify abnormal protein states associated with changes in protein production, loss, hydration, inflammation, or paraproteinemia, but results require clinical context.
options.D: It specifically diagnoses iron-deficiency anemia by measuring iron stored inside circulating red blood cells.

candidate.rationale: Serum total protein reflects major circulating protein fractions and can be altered by several physiologic and disease processes, including changes in production, protein loss, hydration, inflammatory states, and paraproteins. It is not a disease-specific test and does not directly measure GFR or diagnose iron deficiency.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Serum total protein can be abnormal in multiple conditions related to production, loss, hydration, inflammation, or paraproteinemia and is interpreted in clinical context.
candidate.source_version_date: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories test catalog; accessed 2026-08-16
